title: HPVM-HDC: A Heterogeneous Programming System for Accelerating Hyperdimensional Computing
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) programs are manually written in target-specific languages (CUDA, C++, Python) that cannot be retargeted to HDC-specific accelerators (digital ASICs, ReRAM devices), and no programming system enables productive development with efficient code generation across CPUs, GPUs, and multiple HDC accelerators.
motivation: Custom HDC accelerators achieve orders-of-magnitude power efficiency gains but will only see broad adoption if supported by practical, retargetable programming abstractions that eliminate the need to rewrite applications for each hardware target.
method: Programmers write code once in HDC++, a programming language with 24 built-in operations for hyperdimensional computing (hypervector and hypermatrix operations, Hamming distance, cosine similarity, and loop constructs for encoding, training, and inference). The HPVM-HDC compiler translates this code to multiple hardware targets: CPUs, GPUs (via CUDA, cuBLAS, and Thrust), a 40-nanometer digital HDC ASIC (with a Hamming-distance pipeline achieving 0.78 TOPS per watt), and a ReRAM accelerator simulator. To optimize performance, the compiler exploits HDC's tolerance for approximation using automatic binarization (reducing numbers to 1 bit via taint analysis to identify which values can be safely simplified) and reduction perforation (strided or segmented loop skipping for Hamming distance, cosine similarity, and matrix operations over hypervector dimensions).
key_novelty: HDC++'s high-level loop constructs (encoding_loop, training_loop, and inference_loop) can be compiled to different abstraction levels: coarse-grained accelerator instructions for ASICs and ReRAM, or fine-grained CUDA and CPU instructions for GPUs and CPUs, enabling the first execution of complete hyperdimensional computing applications on both a fabricated digital ASIC and a ReRAM accelerator.
contributions: HDC++: first HDC-specific high-level programming language with 24 target-agnostic primitives including coarse-grain stage-level constructs for accelerator targeting
HPVM-HDC: first retargetable compiler for HDC generating code for CPUs, GPUs, a digital ASIC (40nm), and a ReRAM accelerator simulator from a single source
Automatic binarization and reduction perforation compiler optimizations exploiting HDC error resilience, achieving up to 3.4x GPU speedup with marginal accuracy loss
1.17x geomean GPU speedup over optimized CUDA baselines and 1.6x reduction in total lines of code across 5 HDC applications

metrics.speedup: 1.17x geomean over optimized CUDA on GPU; up to 3.4x with approximation optimizations
metrics.other: 1.6x reduction in total LOC across CPU+GPU baselines; first HDC application execution on digital ASIC and ReRAM accelerator

limitations: Approximation optimizations (binarization, reduction perforation) are not automatically selected — the programmer must specify them; automatic selection of optimal approximation configurations is left to future work.
primary_theme: Retargetable HDC programming system with DSL and heterogeneous compiler
